unknown_signal: ^negative-controls: THE HARNESS ITSELF REFUSED TO LOOK$
limits: A THIRD registration on this gate (issue #1129), covering a property neither of the two beside it does: that a gate which REFUSED a verdict is still told apart from one that FELL OVER, now that a case may register the refusal. controls/check-negative-controls asks whether a crashing gate is told from a detecting one (#946); controls/check-negative-controls-unavailable asks whether a silent gate is told from one whose own TOOL is absent (#1117); this one asks whether a silent gate is told from one the INPUT defeated. SEPARATE RATHER THAN TWO MORE CASES ON THE EXISTING CONTROL, and the reason is MEASURED rather than argued: run against this control's known-bad tree, that control's frozen pre-#946 anchor reports UNRESOLVED and exits 1 ('control.json has case(s) with an unknown expect value: [UNKNOWN]') - it predates the expectation entirely. An anchor that exits non-zero on the known-bad input reads as having CAUGHT it, so adding these cases there would report a working control INERT and send someone to replace a perfectly good artifact. Several registrations per gate have been supported since #986. WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH: that the anchor's naive design is the only way to get #1129 wrong. It is one, chosen because it is the one a reasonable person writes on purpose; the other refusals (a marker matching empty output, a clean run, or a detection) are pinned by tests/test_negative_controls.py, which is a different process and the external opinion this harness cannot be for itself. unknown_signal is declared as a string this harness NEVER EMITS, ON PURPOSE - the same decision the control beside it made about unavailable_signal, for the same reason. The honest omission would be 'this gate has no refusal branch', but a control whose subject IS the refusal machinery should exercise the declaration path rather than the omission path, and a pattern that can never match demonstrates that DECLARING the field cannot by itself excuse anything. That is precisely the fail-open the anchor embodies: it parses the field and never consults it.

cases.name: bad-crashing-gate
cases.why: A toy gate that FALLS OVER on the input its control registers as UNKNOWN. The harness must report UNSIGNALLED - a crash is not a refusal - and exit 1.

cases.name: good-unknown-gate
cases.why: The same toy gate with one branch changed: it REFUSES in the words its manifest declares. The harness must reach PASS and exit 0. One branch apart from the known-bad tree, so the pair establishes WHICH distinction the harness is reading.

anchors.why: CONSTRUCTED, reconstructing #1129 IMPLEMENTED NAIVELY rather than an earlier revision of this gate - the naive version never existed as a commit, because the declared-marker requirement landed with the expectation. It is the SHIPPED harness with ONE decision changed, derived from the current file so that every other line is identical: an anchor differing in two places cannot isolate either. (Regenerated during #1129 whenever the harness changed, after counter-model fixes landed in the harness and left the frozen copy differing in four places rather than one - which would have made the demonstration unreadable without changing its verdict, the quieter half of that hazard.) THE ONE DECISION: _observe still PARSES unknown_signal and then never consults it, attributing any non-zero exit that did not announce a finding to a refusal. MEASURED as frozen: it scores the crashing tree PASS/exit 0 where the current harness reports UNSIGNALLED/exit 1, and agrees with the current harness on the known-good tree.
